lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
Date of birth: 2 Nov 1996 | Nationality: American
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Jul 2018 - Aug 2023
- Cut late deliveries from 11% to 7% by excluding weather-delayed shipments from the on-time calculation.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites; my redesign of the slotting rules was rolled out with the floor supervisors and 45 retrained pickers.
- Ran the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations for 12 consecutive quarters, introducing a consensus forecast that cut forecast error from 18% to 11%.
- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots, training 60 drivers and dispatchers and saving 1,800 driver hours a year.
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Improved checkout conversion by 35% after replacing the three-step flow with a one-page flow for all merchants.
- Wrote the requirements and success metrics for dispute self-service, aligning engineering, risk and support; the team shipped it two weeks ahead of plan.
- Interviewed 25 merchants and analysed six months of chargeback data to size annual chargeback losses at 1.1 million dollars, the business case that set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran weekly triage with engineering and support, closing 140 onboarding tickets over the summer and cutting the open-ticket queue by half.
- Measured the onboarding redesign by comparing merchants who opted into the new flow with those who stayed on the old one.
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Launched pickup reminders after 60 user interviews showed students missed pickup windows; weekly active users grew from 400 to 1,150 over the following term.
- Set up a volunteer shift system with two dining halls, filling 95% of pickup slots each week and cutting staff cover shifts from 10 to 2 a week.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Held weekly working sessions with clinic managers on outpatient scheduling across the network.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Halved the time it takes a new merchant to receive a first payment, across 2,300 merchants, by redesigning onboarding.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: Put the more recent Harbor internship before the older Crestline role.
items.because: The experience section should be ordered consistently by date.

items.says: Make the product relevance of the logistics experience clearer.
items.because: Operations and support work compete with the product evidence.

items.says: Consider a short positioning summary.
items.because: The target role and product fit are not immediately clear.

items.says: Add substantive product-related detail to education if available.
items.because: The section shows little directly relevant evidence beyond the projects listed later.

items.says: Check units, time periods and metric formatting for consistency.
Check that the profile link leads to a working, professional page.
items.because: The example-domain link cannot be verified from the text.

items.says: Remove the date of birth and nationality unless required.
items.because: They disclose personal information without showing role-related qualifications.

items.says: Make clear whether the MBA is completed.
items.because: The dates end in June 2025, but its completion status is unclear.

items.says: Excluding weather delays does not demonstrate that late deliveries fell.
items.because: It changes the measurement, not necessarily delivery performance, and may read as KPI manipulation.

items.says: Clarify the basis for the 30% pick-error reduction.
items.because: The scope of the result is hard to assess.

items.says: Distinguish your contribution from the supervisors’ and retrained pickers’ work.
items.because: Attribution is hard to assess.

items.says: Clarify that the forecast-error comparison uses a consistent method and timeframe.
items.because: The quantified forecasting outcome needs to be defensible.

items.says: Explain how the annual driver-hours saving was calculated and whether it was realized or projected.
items.because: The claimed efficiency gain needs to be defensible.

items.says: Give the basis, measurement period and population for the 35% conversion improvement.
items.because: Without that context, the figure is hard to assess, including whether it means relative change or percentage points.

items.says: Clarify whether “all merchants” accurately describes the rollout and measurement.
items.because: It is a very broad scope.

items.says: Add the product impact of dispute self-service if it can be substantiated.
items.because: Shipping ahead of plan alone says less about product value.

items.says: Specify the currency for the 1.1 million figure.
items.because: The current wording leaves it unspecified.

items.says: Clarify whether the chargeback-loss figure is an estimate, annualized figure or measured loss.
items.because: The current wording is ambiguous.

items.says: Make clear how the triage work demonstrates product ownership.
items.because: The bullet risks making the internship look like support operations.

items.says: Distinguish your contribution from the team’s ticket-closing work.
items.because: Attribution of the ticket and queue results is unclear.

items.says: State what the onboarding comparison measured or taught you.
items.because: The bullet describes a method but gives no result.

items.says: Explain the limits of the opt-in comparison rather than treating it as causal evidence.
items.because: Self-selection can bias the comparison, so it does not by itself establish that the redesign caused an outcome.

items.says: Clarify how the pilot-region onboarding result was measured.
items.because: The claimed improvement needs to be defensible.

items.says: Make the project’s first-year timing clear relative to its October 2023 start.
items.because: The launch bullet refers to impact in its first year.

items.says: Substantiate the 9-tonne food-rescue estimate.
items.because: The impact figure needs to be defensible.

items.says: Clarify the period over which weekly active users grew.
items.because: The timeframe for the growth is unclear.

items.says: Clarify whether the user growth can reasonably be attributed to pickup reminders.
items.because: Other changes could explain the increase.

items.says: Give this operational bullet less priority unless it shows meaningful product or process ownership.
items.because: It is less directly product-focused than the research and adoption bullets.

items.says: State what changed because of the weekly working sessions.
items.because: The bullet describes an activity, not an outcome.

items.says: Use active phrasing to make your contribution and the changes clear.
items.because: The passive wording obscures what you did and what changed.

items.says: Give a more concrete result and explain how adoption was established.
items.because: The current description leaves the outcome and adoption vague.

items.says: The merchant first-payment result appears copied from Harbor Payments and misattributed to the hospital practicum.
items.because: It duplicates the onboarding result and is incongruous in a hospital-network project.

items.says: Make clear which listed product skills you have actually applied.
items.because: The skills need support from the experience on the page.

items.says: Verify the A/B-testing claim or remove it if there is no separate randomized-testing experience.
items.because: The described opt-in comparison does not establish an A/B test.

items.says: Add other relevant tools or methods only if you have used them.
items.because: The current tools list is short, and any additions should be discussable in an interview.
